Washing by hand didn't remove the milk smell, but with the wash and sterilization, the tumbler container is clean. - However, pre-washing is essential for severe cases. You need to make sure the dishes are evenly placed. (This can be a bit annoying, and if you put in something like a noodle bowl, the rest won't fit easily, leaving you with limited space.) 3. The 72-hour circulation drying system. It's convenient because you can leave it on while you go out. 4. No installation required, manual water supply. It's a plus because it doesn't require separate installation, but it's also a minus because you have to manually fill 5L of water. This may vary from person to person. Based on my home, it's a plus. The minuses are: 1. It's not very spacious because it's designed to spread the dishes evenly. One noodle bowl can only hold a spoon, a small bowl, and a few cups. It might be a bit cramped for three people. (Of course, if you only put rice and soup bowls in, it might barely fit three people. Adding side dish bowls would be impossible.) However, the outside is larger than the inside, so it might take up a lot of space for one person. I recommend it even if you live alone, as long as you have a large sink. 2. It's a bit noisy. Personally, I think it's louder than a drum washing machine when it's busy. It's probably not ideal for running at night. It's better suited for running it during the day or right before work. 3. It doesn't completely dry. You can hear a fan noise when it's done, but there's still some moisture left. It definitely cleans better (it even removes any residual milk odor from protein shakes!), and it's convenient because you can do other things during that time. However, you still have to do things like frying pans, pots, and cutting boards by hand. And since running the dishwasher takes about 5-6 times longer than just washing dishes, you should probably decide whether to buy one based on your personal lifestyle. I haven't used it for long, so I'm not sure about the electricity bill. I know dishwashers don't use much electricity, but I'm not sure about this one. I run it almost every day, but if my electricity bill goes up, I'll add a review. ------------------------. 6-week review. 1. It doesn't use much electricity. 2. Even regular dishes need to be washed beforehand to remove red pepper powder and other contaminants. 4. It's very loud, especially at night. Conclusion! -> The dishes and cups are washed and sterilized, so they're definitely clean. Good odor removal. Highly recommended for washing cups like tumblers. -> The pre-treatment process can be a hassle, and the washing time is long. -> My electricity bill hasn't changed much since last year. (I'm not sure about the air conditioning in the summer, but my spring electricity bill is similar.) The minuses are: 1. It's not very spacious because it's designed to spread the dishes evenly. One noodle bowl can only hold a spoon, a small bowl, and a few cups. It might be a bit cramped for three people. (Of course, if you only put rice and soup bowls in, it might barely fit three people. Adding side dish bowls would be impossible.) However, the outside is larger than the inside, so it might take up a lot of space for one person. I recommend it even if you live alone, as long as you have a large sink. 2. It's a bit noisy. It doesn't completely dry. You can hear a fan noise when it's done, but there's still some moisture left. It definitely cleans better (it even removes any residual milk odor from protein shakes!), and it's convenient because you can do other things during that time. However, you still have to do things like frying pans, pots, and cutting boards by hand. And since running the dishwasher takes about 5-6 times longer than just washing dishes, you should probably decide whether to buy one based on your personal lifestyle. Even regular dishes need to be washed beforehand to remove red pepper powder and other contaminants. 4. It's very loud, especially at night. Conclusion! -> The dishes and cups are washed and sterilized, so they're definitely clean. Good odor removal. Highly recommended for washing cups like tumblers. -> The pre-treatment process can be a hassle, and the washing time is long. -> My electricity bill hasn't changed much since last year. (I'm not sure about the air conditioning in the summer, but my spring electricity bill is similar.) The 72-hour circulation drying system. It's convenient because you can leave it on while you go out. 4. No installation required, manual water supply. It's a plus because it doesn't require separate installation, but it's also a minus because you have to manually fill 5L of water. This may vary from person to person. Based on my home, it's a plus. The minuses are: 1. It's not very spacious because it's designed to spread the dishes evenly. One noodle bowl can only hold a spoon, a small bowl, and a few cups. It might be a bit cramped for three people. (Of course, if you only put rice and soup bowls in, it might barely fit three people. Adding side dish bowls would be impossible.) However, the outside is larger than the inside, so it might take up a lot of space for one person. I recommend it even if you live alone, as long as you have a large sink. 2. It's a bit noisy. Personally, I think it's louder than a drum washing machine when it's busy. It's probably not ideal for running at night. It's better suited for running it during the day or right before work. 3. It doesn't completely dry. You can hear a fan noise when it's done, but there's still some moisture left. It definitely cleans better (it even removes any residual milk odor from protein shakes!), and it's convenient because you can do other things during that time. However, you still have to do things like frying pans, pots, and cutting boards by hand. And since running the dishwasher takes about 5-6 times longer than just washing dishes, you should probably decide whether to buy one based on your personal lifestyle. I haven't used it for long, so I'm not sure about the electricity bill. I know dishwashers don't use much electricity, but I'm not sure about this one. I run it almost every day, but if my electricity bill goes up, I'll add a review. ------------------------. 6-week review. 1. It doesn't use much electricity. 2. Even regular dishes need to be washed beforehand to remove red pepper powder and other contaminants. 4. It's very loud, especially at night. Conclusion! -> The dishes and cups are washed and sterilized, so they're definitely clean. Good odor removal. Highly recommended for washing cups like tumblers. -> The pre-treatment process can be a hassle, and the washing time is long. -> My electricity bill hasn't changed much since last year. (I'm not sure about the air conditioning in the summer, but my spring electricity bill is similar.) It's a plus because it doesn't require separate installation, but it's also a minus because you have to manually fill 5L of water. This may vary from person to person. Based on my home, it's a plus. The minuses are: 1. It's not very spacious because it's designed to spread the dishes evenly. One noodle bowl can only hold a spoon, a small bowl, and a few cups. It might be a bit cramped for three people. (Of course, if you only put rice and soup bowls in, it might barely fit three people. Adding side dish bowls would be impossible.) However, the outside is larger than the inside, so it might take up a lot of space for one person. I recommend it even if you live alone, as long as you have a large sink. 2. It's a bit noisy. Personally, I think it's louder than a drum washing machine when it's busy. It's probably not ideal for running at night. It's better suited for running it during the day or right before work. 3. It doesn't completely dry. You can hear a fan noise when it's done, but there's still some moisture left. It definitely cleans better (it even removes any residual milk odor from protein shakes!), and it's convenient because you can do other things during that time. However, you still have to do things like frying pans, pots, and cutting boards by hand. And since running the dishwasher takes about 5-6 times longer than just washing dishes, you should probably decide whether to buy one based on your personal lifestyle. I haven't used it for long, so I'm not sure about the electricity bill. I know dishwashers don't use much electricity, but I'm not sure about this one. I run it almost every day, but if my electricity bill goes up, I'll add a review. ------------------------. 6-week review. 1. It doesn't use much electricity. 2. I drink protein shakes, and I wash shake containers and coffee tumblers. It removes odors well. 3. Pots and pans don't fit in the dishwasher, so you have to wash them by hand. Even regular dishes need to be washed beforehand to remove red pepper powder and other contaminants. 4. It's very loud, especially at night. Conclusion! -> The dishes and cups are washed and sterilized, so they're definitely clean. Good odor removal. Highly recommended for washing cups like tumblers. -> The pre-treatment process can be a hassle, and the washing time is long. -> My electricity bill hasn't changed much since last year. (I'm not sure about the air conditioning in the summer, but my spring electricity bill is similar.) Conclusion! -> The dishes and cups are washed and sterilized, so they're definitely clean. Good odor removal. It definitely cleans better (it even removes any residual milk odor from protein shakes!), and it's convenient because you can do other things during that time. However, you still have to do things like frying pans, pots, and cutting boards by hand. And since running the dishwasher takes about 5-6 times longer than just washing dishes, you should probably decide whether to buy one based on your personal lifestyle. Conclusion! -> The dishes and cups are washed and sterilized, so they're definitely clean. Good odor removal. However, the outside is larger than the inside, so it might take up a lot of space for one person. I recommend it even if you live alone, as long as you have a large sink. 2. It's a bit noisy. It definitely cleans better (it even removes any residual milk odor from protein shakes!), and it's convenient because you can do other things during that time. However, you still have to do things like frying pans, pots, and cutting boards by hand. And since running the dishwasher takes about 5-6 times longer than just washing dishes, you should probably decide whether to buy one based on your personal lifestyle. Conclusion! -> The dishes and cups are washed and sterilized, so they're definitely clean. Good odor removal. Highly recommended for washing cups like tumblers. -> The pre-treatment process can be a hassle, and the washing time is long. -> My electricity bill hasn't changed much since last year. Washing by hand didn't remove the milk smell, but with the wash and sterilization, the tumbler container is clean. - However, pre-washing is essential for severe cases. The 72-hour circulation drying system. It's convenient because you can leave it on while you go out. 4. No installation required, manual water supply. It's a plus because it doesn't require separate installation, but it's also a minus because you have to manually fill 5L of water. This may vary from person to person. Based on my home, it's a plus. The minuses are: 1. It's not very spacious because it's designed to spread the dishes evenly. One noodle bowl can only hold a spoon, a small bowl, and a few cups. It might be a bit cramped for three people. (Of course, if you only put rice and soup bowls in, it might barely fit three people. Adding side dish bowls would be impossible.) However, the outside is larger than the inside, so it might take up a lot of space for one person. I recommend it even if you live alone, as long as you have a large sink. 2. It's a bit noisy. Personally, I think it's louder than a drum washing machine when it's busy. It's probably not ideal for running at night. It's better suited for running it during the day or right before work. 3. It doesn't completely dry. You can hear a fan noise when it's done, but there's still some moisture left. It definitely cleans better (it even removes any residual milk odor from protein shakes!), and it's convenient because you can do other things during that time. However, you still have to do things like frying pans, pots, and cutting boards by hand. And since running the dishwasher takes about 5-6 times longer than just washing dishes, you should probably decide whether to buy one based on your personal lifestyle. I haven't used it for long, so I'm not sure about the electricity bill. I know dishwashers don't use much electricity, but I'm not sure about this one. I run it almost every day, but if my electricity bill goes up, I'll add a review. ------------------------. 6-week review. 1. It doesn't use much electricity. 2. I drink protein shakes, and I wash shake containers and coffee tumblers. It removes odors well. 3. Pots and pans don't fit in the dishwasher, so you have to wash them by hand. Even regular dishes need to be washed beforehand to remove red pepper powder and other contaminants. 4. It's very loud, especially at night. Conclusion! -> The dishes and cups are washed and sterilized, so they're definitely clean. Good odor removal. Highly recommended for washing cups like tumblers. -> The pre-treatment process can be a hassle, and the washing time is long. -> My electricity bill hasn't changed much since last year. (I'm not sure about the air conditioning in the summer, but my spring electricity bill is similar.) The minuses are: 1. It's not very spacious because it's designed to spread the dishes evenly. One noodle bowl can only hold a spoon, a small bowl, and a few cups. It might be a bit cramped for three people. (Of course, if you only put rice and soup bowls in, it might barely fit three people. Adding side dish bowls would be impossible.) However, the outside is larger than the inside, so it might take up a lot of space for one person. I recommend it even if you live alone, as long as you have a large sink. 2. It's a bit noisy. Personally, I think it's louder than a drum washing machine when it's busy. It's probably not ideal for running at night. It's better suited for running it during the day or right before work. 3. It doesn't completely dry. You can hear a fan noise when it's done, but there's still some moisture left. It definitely cleans better (it even removes any residual milk odor from protein shakes!), and it's convenient because you can do other things during that time. However, you still have to do things like frying pans, pots, and cutting boards by hand. And since running the dishwasher takes about 5-6 times longer than just washing dishes, you should probably decide whether to buy one based on your personal lifestyle. Even regular dishes need to be washed beforehand to remove red pepper powder and other contaminants. 4. It's very loud, especially at night. Conclusion! -> The dishes and cups are washed and sterilized, so they're definitely clean. Good odor removal. Highly recommended for washing cups like tumblers. -> The pre-treatment process can be a hassle, and the washing time is long. -> My electricity bill hasn't changed much since last year. (I'm not sure about the air conditioning in the summer, but my spring electricity bill is similar.) It's a plus because it doesn't require separate installation, but it's also a minus because you have to manually fill 5L of water. This may vary from person to person. Based on my home, it's a plus. The minuses are: 1. It's not very spacious because it's designed to spread the dishes evenly. One noodle bowl can only hold a spoon, a small bowl, and a few cups. It might be a bit cramped for three people. (Of course, if you only put rice and soup bowls in, it might barely fit three people. Adding side dish bowls would be impossible.) However, the outside is larger than the inside, so it might take up a lot of space for one person. I recommend it even if you live alone, as long as you have a large sink. 2. It's a bit noisy. Personally, I think it's louder than a drum washing machine when it's busy. It's probably not ideal for running at night. It's better suited for running it during the day or right before work. 3. It doesn't completely dry. You can hear a fan noise when it's done, but there's still some moisture left. It definitely cleans better (it even removes any residual milk odor from protein shakes!), and it's convenient because you can do other things during that time. However, you still have to do things like frying pans, pots, and cutting boards by hand. And since running the dishwasher takes about 5-6 times longer than just washing dishes, you should probably decide whether to buy one based on your personal lifestyle. I haven't used it for long, so I'm not sure about the electricity bill. I know dishwashers don't use much electricity, but I'm not sure about this one. I run it almost every day, but if my electricity bill goes up, I'll add a review. ------------------------. 6-week review. 1. It doesn't use much electricity. 2. Even regular dishes need to be washed beforehand to remove red pepper powder and other contaminants. 4. It's very loud, especially at night. Conclusion! -> The dishes and cups are washed and sterilized, so they're definitely clean. Good odor removal. Highly recommended for washing cups like tumblers. -> The pre-treatment process can be a hassle, and the washing time is long. -> My electricity bill hasn't changed much since last year. (I'm not sure about the air conditioning in the summer, but my spring electricity bill is similar.) It's a plus because it doesn't require separate installation, but it's also a minus because you have to manually fill 5L of water. This may vary from person to person. Based on my home, it's a plus. The minuses are: 1. It's not very spacious because it's designed to spread the dishes evenly. One noodle bowl can only hold a spoon, a small bowl, and a few cups. It might be a bit cramped for three people. (Of course, if you only put rice and soup bowls in, it might barely fit three people. Adding side dish bowls would be impossible.) However, the outside is larger than the inside, so it might take up a lot of space for one person. I recommend it even if you live alone, as long as you have a large sink. 2. It's a bit noisy. Personally, I think it's louder than a drum washing machine when it's busy. It's probably not ideal for running at night. It's better suited for running it during the day or right before work. 3. It doesn't completely dry. You can hear a fan noise when it's done, but there's still some moisture left. It definitely cleans better (it even removes any residual milk odor from protein shakes!), and it's convenient because you can do other things during that time. However, you still have to do things like frying pans, pots, and cutting boards by hand. And since running the dishwasher takes about 5-6 times longer than just washing dishes, you should probably decide whether to buy one based on your personal lifestyle. I haven't used it for long, so I'm not sure about the electricity bill. I know dishwashers don't use much electricity, but I'm not sure about this one. I run it almost every day, but if my electricity bill goes up, I'll add a review. ------------------------. 6-week review. 1. It doesn't use much electricity. 2. Even regular dishes need to be washed beforehand to remove red pepper powder and other contaminants. 4. It's very loud, especially at night. Conclusion! -> The dishes and cups are washed and sterilized, so they're definitely clean. Good odor removal. Highly recommended for washing cups like tumblers. -> The pre-treatment process can be a hassle, and the washing time is long. -> My electricity bill hasn't changed much since last year. (I'm not sure about the air conditioning in the summer, but my spring electricity bill is similar.) Comments (English): [ It washes well. ] || ---------------- || This is my first dishwasher. Reviews vary from person to person. I was hesitant to install an expensive dishwasher, so I decided to try a small, easy-to-install dishwasher. The shipping box arrived safely, but it was huge. The shoe cabinet door wouldn't fit, so I opened it from the outside. I just took out the dishwasher and moved it. It's heavy, but not so heavy that a woman couldn't hear it. It's surprisingly large, so it takes up some space. Fortunately, it fits perfectly on one side, which is nice. Before use, there are inlet and drain hoses. Once you install the drain hose, you can also manually inject it, making installation simple. Just use a screwdriver to tighten the plug in the back, so even a woman can install it. The inlet hose can be installed, but I don't like complicated things. It's a bit of a hassle to manually fill it, but it's worth it. You can just put the sink hose into the inlet tank. The included drip tray is surprisingly convenient for filling water. The functions are standard, strong, eco, sterilization, rapid, and preset. Standard, Powerful, Eco, and Sterilize modes take too much time. They take an hour or a little over an hour. Honestly, it's not a large dishwasher. Since it only takes 60-80 minutes for a few dishes, I'm worried about the electricity bill. I also wonder if it's really practical. The quick 30-minute cycle is decent. Most dishes are washed very cleanly on the quick mode. However, the quick mode is disappointing because there's no drying function at all. In that case, I'd rather have a separate drying function. And manual time control would be nice, too. The 20-30 minute easy wash mode is perfect. While the capacity is for three people, it's a good size for one or two people living alone, or for newlyweds. It probably won't fit a pot, but it's perfect for simple dishes like rice, soup, spoons, chopsticks, and cups. Another major drawback is the lack of a lock. Since we have children, I only use it when the kids aren't around. The dishwasher door can't be opened, but the buttons are easy to press. It keeps pressing down on the dishwasher. Unplug it when not in use. If you're worried about the dishwasher running for 30 to 60 minutes, you have to keep an eye on it. The cleaning power is a misconception, considering the dishwashers of the past! These days, dishwashers really do a great job of cleaning. Even a tiny amount of detergent gets it really clean. Finally, the only real disappointment is that even with a dishwasher, you still have to wash the dishes! I tend to use plastic dishes more often than ceramic ones, but they can't all fit in the dishwasher. The dishes get scratched and damaged after a few cycles. They feel like they're going bad. Fragile dishes crack. The insides feel like they're cracked. Even dishes with bands can't fit in. Again, you have to buy dishwasher-specific dishes. Surprisingly, many dishes don't fit, which is a shame. This is an honest review written after receiving the product for free as part of a Coupang Experience Group event. Unplug it when not in use. If you're worried about the dishwasher running for 30 to 60 minutes, you have to keep an eye on it. The cleaning power is a misconception, considering the dishwashers of the past! These days, dishwashers really do a great job of cleaning. Even a tiny amount of detergent gets it really clean. Finally, the only real disappointment is that even with a dishwasher, you still have to wash the dishes! I tend to use plastic dishes more often than ceramic ones, but they can't all fit in the dishwasher. The dishes get scratched and damaged after a few cycles. They feel like they're going bad. Fragile dishes crack. The insides feel like they're cracked. Even dishes with bands can't fit in. Again, you have to buy dishwasher-specific dishes. Comments (English): [ It washes well. ] || ---------------- || This is my first dishwasher. Reviews vary from person to person. I was hesitant to install an expensive dishwasher, so I decided to try a small, easy-to-install dishwasher. The shipping box arrived safely, but it was huge. It's surprisingly large, so it takes up some space. Fortunately, it fits perfectly on one side, which is nice. Before use, there are inlet and drain hoses. Once you install the drain hose, you can also manually inject it, making installation simple. Just use a screwdriver to tighten the plug in the back, so even a woman can install it. The inlet hose can be installed, but I don't like complicated things. It's a bit of a hassle to manually fill it, but it's worth it. You can just put the sink hose into the inlet tank. The included drip tray is surprisingly convenient for filling water. The functions are standard, strong, eco, sterilization, rapid, and preset. Standard, Powerful, Eco, and Sterilize modes take too much time. They take an hour or a little over an hour. Honestly, it's not a large dishwasher. Since it only takes 60-80 minutes for a few dishes, I'm worried about the electricity bill. I also wonder if it's really practical. The quick 30-minute cycle is decent. Most dishes are washed very cleanly on the quick mode. However, the quick mode is disappointing because there's no drying function at all. In that case, I'd rather have a separate drying function. And manual time control would be nice, too. The 20-30 minute easy wash mode is perfect. While the capacity is for three people, it's a good size for one or two people living alone, or for newlyweds. It probably won't fit a pot, but it's perfect for simple dishes like rice, soup, spoons, chopsticks, and cups. Another major drawback is the lack of a lock. Since we have children, I only use it when the kids aren't around. The dishwasher door can't be opened, but the buttons are easy to press. It keeps pressing down on the dishwasher. Unplug it when not in use. If you're worried about the dishwasher running for 30 to 60 minutes, you have to keep an eye on it. The cleaning power is a misconception, considering the dishwashers of the past! These days, dishwashers really do a great job of cleaning. Even a tiny amount of detergent gets it really clean. Finally, the only real disappointment is that even with a dishwasher, you still have to wash the dishes! I tend to use plastic dishes more often than ceramic ones, but they can't all fit in the dishwasher. The dishes get scratched and damaged after a few cycles. They feel like they're going bad. Fragile dishes crack. The insides feel like they're cracked. Even dishes with bands can't fit in. Again, you have to buy dishwasher-specific dishes. Surprisingly, many dishes don't fit, which is a shame. This is an honest review written after receiving the product for free as part of a Coupang Experience Group event. Most dishes are washed very cleanly on the quick mode. However, the quick mode is disappointing because there's no drying function at all. In that case, I'd rather have a separate drying function. Since we have children, I only use it when the kids aren't around. The dishwasher door can't be opened, but the buttons are easy to press. It keeps pressing down on the dishwasher. Unplug it when not in use. If you're worried about the dishwasher running for 30 to 60 minutes, you have to keep an eye on it. The cleaning power is a misconception, considering the dishwashers of the past! These days, dishwashers really do a great job of cleaning. Even a tiny amount of detergent gets it really clean. Finally, the only real disappointment is that even with a dishwasher, you still have to wash the dishes! I tend to use plastic dishes more often than ceramic ones, but they can't all fit in the dishwasher. The dishes get scratched and damaged after a few cycles. They feel like they're going bad. Fragile dishes crack. The insides feel like they're cracked. Even dishes with bands can't fit in. Again, you have to buy dishwasher-specific dishes. Comments (English): [ It washes well. ] || ---------------- || This is my first dishwasher. Reviews vary from person to person. I was hesitant to install an expensive dishwasher, so I decided to try a small, easy-to-install dishwasher. The shipping box arrived safely, but it was huge. The shoe cabinet door wouldn't fit, so I opened it from the outside. I just took out the dishwasher and moved it. It's heavy, but not so heavy that a woman couldn't hear it. It's surprisingly large, so it takes up some space. Fortunately, it fits perfectly on one side, which is nice. Before use, there are inlet and drain hoses. Once you install the drain hose, you can also manually inject it, making installation simple. Just use a screwdriver to tighten the plug in the back, so even a woman can install it. The inlet hose can be installed, but I don't like complicated things. It's a bit of a hassle to manually fill it, but it's worth it. You can just put the sink hose into the inlet tank. The included drip tray is surprisingly convenient for filling water. The functions are standard, strong, eco, sterilization, rapid, and preset. Standard, Powerful, Eco, and Sterilize modes take too much time. They take an hour or a little over an hour. Honestly, it's not a large dishwasher. Since it only takes 60-80 minutes for a few dishes, I'm worried about the electricity bill. I also wonder if it's really practical. The quick 30-minute cycle is decent. Most dishes are washed very cleanly on the quick mode. However, the quick mode is disappointing because there's no drying function at all. In that case, I'd rather have a separate drying function. And manual time control would be nice, too. The 20-30 minute easy wash mode is perfect. While the capacity is for three people, it's a good size for one or two people living alone, or for newlyweds. It probably won't fit a pot, but it's perfect for simple dishes like rice, soup, spoons, chopsticks, and cups. Another major drawback is the lack of a lock. Since we have children, I only use it when the kids aren't around. The dishwasher door can't be opened, but the buttons are easy to press. It keeps pressing down on the dishwasher. Unplug it when not in use. If you're worried about the dishwasher running for 30 to 60 minutes, you have to keep an eye on it. The cleaning power is a misconception, considering the dishwashers of the past! These days, dishwashers really do a great job of cleaning. Even a tiny amount of detergent gets it really clean. Finally, the only real disappointment is that even with a dishwasher, you still have to wash the dishes! I tend to use plastic dishes more often than ceramic ones, but they can't all fit in the dishwasher. The dishes get scratched and damaged after a few cycles. They feel like they're going bad. Fragile dishes crack. The insides feel like they're cracked. Even dishes with bands can't fit in. Again, you have to buy dishwasher-specific dishes. Surprisingly, many dishes don't fit, which is a shame. This is an honest review written after receiving the product for free as part of a Coupang Experience Group event. Since it only takes 60-80 minutes for a few dishes, I'm worried about the electricity bill. I also wonder if it's really practical. The quick 30-minute cycle is decent. Since we have children, I only use it when the kids aren't around. The dishwasher door can't be opened, but the buttons are easy to press. It keeps pressing down on the dishwasher. Unplug it when not in use. If you're worried about the dishwasher running for 30 to 60 minutes, you have to keep an eye on it. The cleaning power is a misconception, considering the dishwashers of the past! These days, dishwashers really do a great job of cleaning. Even a tiny amount of detergent gets it really clean. Finally, the only real disappointment is that even with a dishwasher, you still have to wash the dishes! I tend to use plastic dishes more often than ceramic ones, but they can't all fit in the dishwasher. The dishes get scratched and damaged after a few cycles. They feel like they're going bad. Fragile dishes crack. The insides feel like they're cracked. Even dishes with bands can't fit in. Again, you have to buy dishwasher-specific dishes. It's surprisingly large, so it takes up some space. Fortunately, it fits perfectly on one side, which is nice. Before use, there are inlet and drain hoses. The inlet hose can be installed, but I don't like complicated things. It's a bit of a hassle to manually fill it, but it's worth it. You can just put the sink hose into the inlet tank. The included drip tray is surprisingly convenient for filling water. The functions are standard, strong, eco, sterilization, rapid, and preset. Standard, Powerful, Eco, and Sterilize modes take too much time. They take an hour or a little over an hour. Honestly, it's not a large dishwasher. Since it only takes 60-80 minutes for a few dishes, I'm worried about the electricity bill. I also wonder if it's really practical. The quick 30-minute cycle is decent. Most dishes are washed very cleanly on the quick mode. However, the quick mode is disappointing because there's no drying function at all. In that case, I'd rather have a separate drying function. And manual time control would be nice, too. The 20-30 minute easy wash mode is perfect. While the capacity is for three people, it's a good size for one or two people living alone, or for newlyweds. It probably won't fit a pot, but it's perfect for simple dishes like rice, soup, spoons, chopsticks, and cups. Another major drawback is the lack of a lock. Since we have children, I only use it when the kids aren't around. The dishwasher door can't be opened, but the buttons are easy to press. It keeps pressing down on the dishwasher. Unplug it when not in use. If you're worried about the dishwasher running for 30 to 60 minutes, you have to keep an eye on it. The cleaning power is a misconception, considering the dishwashers of the past! These days, dishwashers really do a great job of cleaning. Even a tiny amount of detergent gets it really clean. Finally, the only real disappointment is that even with a dishwasher, you still have to wash the dishes! I tend to use plastic dishes more often than ceramic ones, but they can't all fit in the dishwasher. The dishes get scratched and damaged after a few cycles. They feel like they're going bad. Fragile dishes crack. The insides feel like they're cracked. Even dishes with bands can't fit in. Again, you have to buy dishwasher-specific dishes. Surprisingly, many dishes don't fit, which is a shame. This is an honest review written after receiving the product for free as part of a Coupang Experience Group event. It's surprisingly large, so it takes up some space. Fortunately, it fits perfectly on one side, which is nice. Before use, there are inlet and drain hoses. The inlet hose can be installed, but I don't like complicated things. It's a bit of a hassle to manually fill it, but it's worth it. You can just put the sink hose into the inlet tank. The included drip tray is surprisingly convenient for filling water. The functions are standard, strong, eco, sterilization, rapid, and preset. Standard, Powerful, Eco, and Sterilize modes take too much time. They take an hour or a little over an hour. Honestly, it's not a large dishwasher. Since it only takes 60-80 minutes for a few dishes, I'm worried about the electricity bill. I also wonder if it's really practical. The quick 30-minute cycle is decent. Most dishes are washed very cleanly on the quick mode. However, the quick mode is disappointing because there's no drying function at all. In that case, I'd rather have a separate drying function. And manual time control would be nice, too. The 20-30 minute easy wash mode is perfect. While the capacity is for three people, it's a good size for one or two people living alone, or for newlyweds. It probably won't fit a pot, but it's perfect for simple dishes like rice, soup, spoons, chopsticks, and cups. Another major drawback is the lack of a lock. Since we have children, I only use it when the kids aren't around. The dishwasher door can't be opened, but the buttons are easy to press. It keeps pressing down on the dishwasher. Unplug it when not in use. If you're worried about the dishwasher running for 30 to 60 minutes, you have to keep an eye on it. The cleaning power is a misconception, considering the dishwashers of the past! These days, dishwashers really do a great job of cleaning. Even a tiny amount of detergent gets it really clean. Finally, the only real disappointment is that even with a dishwasher, you still have to wash the dishes! I tend to use plastic dishes more often than ceramic ones, but they can't all fit in the dishwasher. The dishes get scratched and damaged after a few cycles. They feel like they're going bad. Fragile dishes crack. The insides feel like they're cracked. Even dishes with bands can't fit in. Again, you have to buy dishwasher-specific dishes. Surprisingly, many dishes don't fit, which is a shame. This is an honest review written after receiving the product for free as part of a Coupang Experience Group event. Comments (English): [ It washes well. ] || ---------------- || This is my first dishwasher. Reviews vary from person to person. I was hesitant to install an expensive dishwasher, so I decided to try a small, easy-to-install dishwasher. The shipping box arrived safely, but it was huge. The shoe cabinet door wouldn't fit, so I opened it from the outside. I just took out the dishwasher and moved it. It's heavy, but not so heavy that a woman couldn't hear it. It's surprisingly large, so it takes up some space. Fortunately, it fits perfectly on one side, which is nice. Before use, there are inlet and drain hoses. Once you install the drain hose, you can also manually inject it, making installation simple. Just use a screwdriver to tighten the plug in the back, so even a woman can install it. The inlet hose can be installed, but I don't like complicated things. It's a bit of a hassle to manually fill it, but it's worth it. You can just put the sink hose into the inlet tank. The included drip tray is surprisingly convenient for filling water. The functions are standard, strong, eco, sterilization, rapid, and preset. Standard, Powerful, Eco, and Sterilize modes take too much time. They take an hour or a little over an hour. Honestly, it's not a large dishwasher. Since it only takes 60-80 minutes for a few dishes, I'm worried about the electricity bill. I also wonder if it's really practical. The quick 30-minute cycle is decent. Most dishes are washed very cleanly on the quick mode. However, the quick mode is disappointing because there's no drying function at all. In that case, I'd rather have a separate drying function. And manual time control would be nice, too. The 20-30 minute easy wash mode is perfect. While the capacity is for three people, it's a good size for one or two people living alone, or for newlyweds. It probably won't fit a pot, but it's perfect for simple dishes like rice, soup, spoons, chopsticks, and cups. Another major drawback is the lack of a lock. Since we have children, I only use it when the kids aren't around. The dishwasher door can't be opened, but the buttons are easy to press. It keeps pressing down on the dishwasher. Unplug it when not in use. If you're worried about the dishwasher running for 30 to 60 minutes, you have to keep an eye on it. The cleaning power is a misconception, considering the dishwashers of the past! These days, dishwashers really do a great job of cleaning. Even a tiny amount of detergent gets it really clean. Finally, the only real disappointment is that even with a dishwasher, you still have to wash the dishes! I tend to use plastic dishes more often than ceramic ones, but they can't all fit in the dishwasher. The dishes get scratched and damaged after a few cycles. They feel like they're going bad. Fragile dishes crack. The insides feel like they're cracked. Even dishes with bands can't fit in. Again, you have to buy dishwasher-specific dishes. Surprisingly, many dishes don't fit, which is a shame. This is an honest review written after receiving the product for free as part of a Coupang Experience Group event. Sentence (English): We have had the dishwasher for about 2 weeks now.
Comments (English): [ Great in the few weeks we have owned it ] || ---------------- || We have had the dishwasher for about 2 weeks now. We picked it because it had the same basket layout as my old, Kenmore machine and I knew how to load it. The third upper rack is new for us and we have found it helpful. I use it mostly for food storage containers, knives, serving spoons and drink lids. However, adding the 3rd upper basket does lower the other two baskets. which might make it difficult for someone with a bad back to load and unload. When open, the door is much closer to the ground. I am able to wash my 32 oz cups on the middle rack and still have enough height for cutting boards and pots on the lowest level. We rinse our dishes because there are only 2 of us and it takes several days to get a full load. The dishes have come out clean. I like the fact that I can move the silverware basket to different locations. front, back, or side. Also, that it will come apart too. Because the door doesn't have a lock, you must tug on the door to get it to open. The door stops whenever you stop pulling. so it might be open just a few inches, to a foot or fully open. You must push the door down to get it at the 90 degree angle to pull out rack. Not sure that I like that feature. it is low and I am getting older. I never timed my old dishwasher. I was surprised to see that this one runs about 3 hours for a normal load. Can run over 8 hours for a heavy load! There is a timer to tell you how long it will run for each cycle. my old dishwasher didn't have that. so it is different to see it. You must open door to see it but nice to know the time left if you need to add an item after you start it.

I am extremely disappointed with this product and the lack of support from both the manufacturer and retailer.

When I reached out to Costco Concierge Service, I was informed that the manufacturer warranty did not cover this problem, and I would have to pay for the service call and any necessary repairs. I did some research online and discovered that this issue has been known for several years. While LG used to cover it under warranty, even replacement control panels are likely to crack again in a short period of time, leading to the manufacturer discontinuing the coverage. I was told that LG would contact me regarding the issue, but only their AD department reached out, and after 7 business days of waiting, I reached out to Costco again. Unfortunately, I was told that I could not return the product since it had passed the 90-day return window and would have to go through the warranty process. This situation has become an endless cycle of bouncing between the Costco customer service department, the concierge department, and LG without any resolution. I am extremely disappointed with this product and the lack of support from both the manufacturer and retailer.

Sentence (English): Ho…kay, Our house is well sprinkled with LG appliances.
Comments (English): [ Mine died an early death ] || ---------------- || Ho…kay, Our house is well sprinkled with LG appliances. There's an LG washer & dryer, dishwasher, plus an old LG Kimchi refrigerator. We bought a model LDT567 dishwasher three years ago. Generally it's held up fairly well, but then it's only used once a day with pre-rinsed dishes, no pots & pans, and prem-o Cascade. I can't knock LG quality, but I do have a serious bone to pick with their product support Two weeks ago, the dishwasher started making a buzzing/grating noice during the wash cycle. Anyone ever looked into dishwasher bowels knows they're mainly a metal / plastic box with a few hoses & solenoids to let water in or out. There's some electronics for turning the thing on and off, and one drive motor which squirts dishwater on your dinner plates and glasses. Basically it's more a big squirt gun than technical genius. So when this t gawd awful noise turned up during the wash cycle, it was a pretty safe bet it was the one and only drive motor making the noise. Probably a failing bearing, but I digress. We called LG Support who suggested running an empty load with a cup of vinegar. We all sat on the phone enduring the racket to prove it can clean vinegar. If anything it got louder. After a couple days, the washer gave out showing an “LE” error. The user manual says it's motor related (real shocker there! ) and back to the support number. The overall warranty is only for one year, BUT! If you read really close their drive motor is warranted for ten! We're back on LG's phone doorstep. Over the next two days and three calls we were handed off to at least five “specialist technicians”. All had us run the exact same diagnostic of resetting the power and and restart. All of which got the same LE code, but now we started smelling that acrid burnt electrical wire odor. Number five culminated in a few beeps, a sizzle, a crackle, and a fizzy pop, followed by the unit powering off …forever, plus us throwing all the windows open from the burning stench. So we're coughing on the phone telling the technician what happened. The thing's dead and what does he want us to do next? He wants us to run the test…AGAIN! These people are either totally whacked or incredibly brilliant. Of course the warranted motor's is toast, but now so are a number of other not-warranted parts as well. Here we sit with a stinky kitchen, a dishwasher requiring expensive repairs, and both warranty and dishwasher up in smoke. Up side is now manual pre-rinse or plain hand wash, what's the difference? I'll throw in a few observational nuggets: In order to receive warranty service, it must be done by an LG certified technician. Since we live in the wild outbacks of coastal San Diego, a local "authorized warranty" repair doesn't exist. Maybe the next bigger town over, LA? LG had to FIND someone (anyone) who'd take a look at their “high tech”. If someone did come out, we'd pay for their time just to look at it, then again a second one to replace the part… plus whatever else went up in smoke. For an $800 appliance the labor alone was shaping up to over $300 not including newly trashed and unwarranted parts. We realized we'd lost this battle. Sanity set in. Who wants an appliance which may or may not have caught fire even if blessed by a “certified technician”. My California fire insurance premium is too expensive as is. I have absolutely zero problems with Lowes. We buy tons of house parts from them, but take a hard look at LG comments in other negative reviews. They're basically boilerplate “Oh, so sorry…We're trying to improve”. I wouldn't be surprised it's a computer program filling these in and tweaking the wording. My advice is LG “probably” makes a respectable dishwasher. Bad parts occasionally slip into even the best (most expensive) machinery. So Caveat Emptor (buyer beware), should your LG appliance break prematurely. Your options are either fix it yourself or run to the store for a replacement. LG support looks worse than non-existent, bordering on the dangerous. Sorry, if this was a bit long.

Generally it's held up fairly well, but then it's only used once a day with pre-rinsed dishes, no pots & pans, and prem-o Cascade. I can't knock LG quality, but I do have a serious bone to pick with their product support Two weeks ago, the dishwasher started making a buzzing/grating noice during the wash cycle. Anyone ever looked into dishwasher bowels knows they're mainly a metal / plastic box with a few hoses & solenoids to let water in or out. There's some electronics for turning the thing on and off, and one drive motor which squirts dishwater on your dinner plates and glasses. Basically it's more a big squirt gun than technical genius. So when this t gawd awful noise turned up during the wash cycle, it was a pretty safe bet it was the one and only drive motor making the noise. Probably a failing bearing, but I digress. We called LG Support who suggested running an empty load with a cup of vinegar. We all sat on the phone enduring the racket to prove it can clean vinegar. If anything it got louder. After a couple days, the washer gave out showing an “LE” error. The user manual says it's motor related (real shocker there! ) and back to the support number. The overall warranty is only for one year, BUT! If you read really close their drive motor is warranted for ten! We're back on LG's phone doorstep. Over the next two days and three calls we were handed off to at least five “specialist technicians”. All had us run the exact same diagnostic of resetting the power and and restart. All of which got the same LE code, but now we started smelling that acrid burnt electrical wire odor. Number five culminated in a few beeps, a sizzle, a crackle, and a fizzy pop, followed by the unit powering off …forever, plus us throwing all the windows open from the burning stench. These people are either totally whacked or incredibly brilliant. Of course the warranted motor's is toast, but now so are a number of other not-warranted parts as well. Here we sit with a stinky kitchen, a dishwasher requiring expensive repairs, and both warranty and dishwasher up in smoke. Up side is now manual pre-rinse or plain hand wash, what's the difference? Since we live in the wild outbacks of coastal San Diego, a local "authorized warranty" repair doesn't exist. Maybe the next bigger town over, LA? LG had to FIND someone (anyone) who'd take a look at their “high tech”. If someone did come out, we'd pay for their time just to look at it, then again a second one to replace the part… plus whatever else went up in smoke. For an $800 appliance the labor alone was shaping up to over $300 not including newly trashed and unwarranted parts. We realized we'd lost this battle. Sanity set in. Who wants an appliance which may or may not have caught fire even if blessed by a “certified technician”. My California fire insurance premium is too expensive as is. I have absolutely zero problems with Lowes. We buy tons of house parts from them, but take a hard look at LG comments in other negative reviews. They're basically boilerplate “Oh, so sorry…We're trying to improve”. I wouldn't be surprised it's a computer program filling these in and tweaking the wording. My advice is LG “probably” makes a respectable dishwasher. Bad parts occasionally slip into even the best (most expensive) machinery. So Caveat Emptor (buyer beware), should your LG appliance break prematurely. Your options are either fix it yourself or run to the store for a replacement. LG support looks worse than non-existent, bordering on the dangerous. Sorry, if this was a bit long.

Generally it’s held up fairly well, but then it’s only used once a day with pre-rinsed dishes, no pots & pans, and prem-o Cascade. I can’t knock LG quality, but I do have a serious bone to pick with their product support  Two weeks ago, the dishwasher started making a buzzing/grating noice during the wash cycle.  Anyone ever looked into dishwasher bowels knows they're mainly a metal / plastic box with a few hoses & solenoids to let water in or out.  There’s some electronics for turning the thing on and off, and one drive motor which squirts dishwater on your dinner plates and glasses. Basically it’s more a big squirt gun than technical genius.  So when this t gawd awful noise turned up during the wash cycle, it was a pretty safe bet it was the one and only drive motor making the noise.  Probably a failing bearing, but I digress.  We called LG Support who suggested running an empty load with a cup of vinegar. We all sat on the phone  enduring the racket to prove it can clean vinegar. If anything it got louder.  After a couple days, the washer gave out showing an “LE” error.  The user manual says it’s motor related (real shocker there!) and back to the support number.  The overall warranty is only for one year, BUT! If you read really close their drive motor is warranted for ten! We’re back on LG’s phone doorstep.  Over the next two days and three calls we were handed off to at least five “specialist technicians”.  All had us run the exact same diagnostic of resetting the power and and restart.  All of which got the same LE code, but now we started smelling that acrid burnt electrical wire odor.  Number five culminated in a few beeps, a sizzle, a crackle, and a fizzy pop, followed by the unit powering off …forever,  plus us throwing all the windows open from the burning stench.  So we’re coughing on the phone telling the technician what happened. The thing’s dead and what does he want us to do next?  He wants us to run the test…AGAIN!  These people are either totally whacked or incredibly brilliant.  Of course the warranted motor’s is toast, but now so are a number of other not-warranted parts as well. Here we sit with a stinky kitchen, a dishwasher requiring expensive repairs, and both warranty and dishwasher up in smoke.  Up side is now manual pre-rinse or plain hand wash, what’s the difference? I’ll throw in a few observational nuggets:  In order to receive warranty service, it must be done by an LG certified technician.  Since we live in the wild outbacks of coastal San Diego, a local 'authorized warranty' repair doesn't exist. Maybe the next bigger town over, LA?  LG had to FIND someone (anyone) who’d take a look at their “high tech”. If someone did come out, we’d pay for their time just to look at it, then again a second one to replace the part… plus whatever else went up in smoke. For an $800 appliance the labor alone was shaping up to over $300 not including newly trashed and unwarranted parts. We realized we’d lost this battle.  Sanity set in. Who wants an appliance which may or may not have caught fire even if blessed by a “certified technician”.  My California fire insurance premium is too expensive as is. I have absolutely zero problems with Lowes.  We buy tons of house parts from them, but take a hard look at LG comments in other negative reviews. My advice is LG “probably” makes a respectable dishwasher. Bad parts occasionally slip into even the  best (most expensive) machinery.  So Caveat Emptor (buyer beware), should your LG appliance break prematurely. Your options are either fix it yourself or run to the store for a replacement.  LG support looks worse than non-existent, bordering on the dangerous.  Sorry, if this was a bit long....

The overall warranty is only for one year, BUT! If you read really close their drive motor is warranted for ten! We're back on LG's phone doorstep. Over the next two days and three calls we were handed off to at least five “specialist technicians”. All had us run the exact same diagnostic of resetting the power and and restart. Sentence (English): We recently got this dishwasher.
Comments (English): [ Fine built-in dishwasher ] || ---------------- || We recently got this dishwasher. We were pleasantly surprised. Despite the same dimensions as the previous one, we can now fit more in it. This is largely due to the cutlery drawer. This gives you more space in the bottom drawer. The various functions are easy to use. The extra drying works well for us with our children's plastic items. We also really like the fact that you can set the door to open automatically so that it can dry even further. We didn't find the manual very clear, but a little fiddling with the functions and you'll soon get the hang of it. The noise level is fine as far as we're concerned (open kitchen). The lights in the machine give it a luxurious look, which is always nice of course. It's also nice that the middle rack is easily adjustable so that you can adjust it to the size of the plates you use.
Comments (Original): [ Fijne inbouwvaatwasser ] || ---------------- || Sinds kort hebben we deze vaatwasser. We zijn blij verrast. Ondanks dezelfde afmetingen als de vorige, kunnen we nu toch meer erin kwijt. Dit heeft voor een groot gedeelte te maken met de besteklade. Hierdoor heb je meer ruimte in de onderste lade. De verschillende functies zijn fijn te gebruiken. Het extra drogen werkt bij ons goed met de plastic spullen van onze kinderen. Ook vinden we het hierbij erg fijn dat je kunt instellen dat de deur vanzelf open gaat zodat het nog verder kan drogen. We vonden de handleiding niet heel duidelijk, maar even stoeien met de functies en dan heb je het al snel door. Het geluidsniveau is wat ons betreft prima (open keuken)De lichten in de machine geven het een luxe uitstraling, dat is altijd leuk natuurlijk. Ook is het fijn dat het middelste rek goed verstelbaar is zodat je het kunt aanpassen aan de grote van de borden die je gebruikt.
